facts.statement: The genus Abyssosaurus was described by Alexander Yu Berezin in 2011.
facts.quote: authority: Berezin, 2011

facts.statement: Fossils of Abyssosaurus date to the Early Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Early Cretaceous,

facts.statement: The type species, A. nataliae, was named by Alexander Yu Berezin in 2011 after his wife, Nataliya Berezina.
facts.quote: It was described in 2011 by Alexander Yu Berezin, who named its type species, A. nataliae, after his wife and colleague, Nataliya Berezina.

facts.statement: Vasily V. Mita discovered a partial plesiosaur skeleton in Chuvashia, Russia, in 1992.
facts.quote: In 1992, Russian palaeontologist Vasily V. Mita discovered the partial skeleton of a plesiosaur around the left tributary of the Sura River, in Chuvashia, Russia.

facts.statement: The strata containing the fossils are dated to the late or upper Hauterivian age of the Early Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Strata from that location, belonging to the Speetoniceras versicolor Subzone, have been dated to the late/upper Hauterivian age of the Early Cretaceous.

facts.statement: Additional remains were discovered in 1998, expanding the initial collection of twenty cervical vertebrae.
facts.quote: Twenty cervical (neck) vertebrae were collected at first, though, in 1998, additional remains were discovered.

facts.statement: In 2011, Alexander Yu Berezin designated the specimen as the holotype for the new species Abyssosaurus nataliae.
facts.quote: In 2011, the specimen was described by Alexander Yu Berezin, who designated it as the holotype of a new genus and species of plesiosaur, Abyssosaurus nataliae.

facts.statement: Berezin published further papers on the cranial anatomy of Abyssosaurus in 2018 and 2019.
facts.quote: Accordingly, in 2018, Berezin published a second paper, discussing Abyssosaurus' cranial anatomy, followed by a third in 2019.

facts.statement: Abyssosaurus was considered aberrant when compared to other members of the family Cryptoclididae.
facts.quote: Abyssosaurus was aberrant compared to other cryptoclidids.

facts.statement: The skull was unusually short and triangular compared to other plesiosaurs, and it featured very large eye sockets.
facts.quote: Its skull was unusually short and triangular in comparison to that of other plesiosaurs, and its eye sockets were very large.

facts.statement: Parts of the skeleton retain juvenile traits known as paedomorphosis, a condition seen in various deep-sea vertebrates.
facts.quote: Parts of its overall skeleton retain juvenile traits, a condition known as paedomorphosis which is observed in various deep-sea vertebrates.

facts.statement: The gastralia and flippers were very robust due to pachyostosis, which would have reduced buoyancy.
facts.quote: Parts of the gastralia (abdominal ribs) and flippers were very robust, an example of pachyostosis which would have made it less buoyant.

facts.statement: Abyssosaurus had an estimated body length of 6.7 to 7 meters and a body mass of 1.24 metric tons.
facts.quote: Abyssosaurus was a large plesiosaur with an estimated total body length of 6.7 - 7 m, with roughly half of its length consisting of its neck, and body mass of 1.24 MT.

facts.statement: Aside from Muraenosaurus, Abyssosaurus is the only cryptoclidid known to preserve a prootic bone, which is more massive in Abyssosaurus.
facts.quote: Abyssosaurus is the only cryptoclidid, aside from Muraenosaurus, to preserve a prootic; in Abyssosaurus, it is more massive than in that taxon.

facts.statement: The exact number of teeth in Abyssosaurus is unknown.
facts.quote: It is not known how many teeth Abyssosaurus had.

facts.statement: The neck column is incomplete, preserving only forty-four vertebrae.
facts.quote: The cervical (neck) column of Abyssosaurus is not known in its entirety, preserving only forty-four vertebrae.

facts.statement: There were twenty dorsal vertebrae, or twenty-three if pectoral vertebrae are included.
facts.quote: Twenty dorsal (body) vertebrae were present, or twenty-three if the pectoral vertebrae are counted.

facts.statement: The number of vertebrae in the tail is unknown.
facts.quote: It is not known how many vertebrae were present in the tail.

facts.statement: The gastralia were unusually thickened, particularly in the center.
facts.quote: Unusually, the gastralia (abdominal ribs) were thickened, particularly in the centre.

facts.statement: The clavicles were greatly atrophied.
facts.quote: The clavicles of Abyssosaurus were greatly atrophied.

facts.statement: Berezin suggested the front flippers were used for steering and stabilization while the hind flippers were used for propulsion.
facts.quote: Due to the morphological disparity between the front and hind flippers, Berezin suggested that the front set was probably used for steering and stabilisation, while the hind set was used for propulsion.

facts.statement: Berezin initially suggested Abyssosaurus was an aberrant member of the subfamily Aristonectinae within Cryptocleidoidea.
facts.quote: In his paper describing Abyssosaurus, Berezin suggested that it was an aberrant member of Aristonectinae, then a family of its own (Aristonectinae) within Cryptocleidoidea.

facts.statement: Later studies concluded that A. nataliae was a colymbosaurine, sister to Colymbosaurus, rather than an aristonectine.
facts.quote: They concluded that, instead of being an aristonectine, A. nataliae was instead a colymbosaurine, sister to Colymbosaurus proper.

facts.statement: The broad thorax indicates a large lung volume, suggesting it could hold its breath for extended periods.
facts.quote: Its thorax was very broad, indicating a very large lung volume and suggests that it held its breath for extended periods of time.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Abyssosaurus was a basal aristonectid or related to Colymbosaurus, with later studies supporting the latter.
facts.quote: While Berezin initially believed that Abyssosaurus was a basal aristonectid, part of a lineage whose later members evolved into giant filter-feeders, later studies have concluded that it was instead related to Colymbosaurus.

facts.statement: Fossil remains tentatively identified as a fetus were found alongside the holotype, suggesting the species reproduced by giving birth to live young.
facts.quote: Alongside the holotype of Abyssosaurus were remains tentatively attributed to a foetus of the same taxon, though this specimen has yet to be described.

facts.statement: Abyssosaurus was an extinct plesiosaur that lived during the Early Cretaceous in what is now Russia.
facts.quote: Abyssosaurus es un género extinto de plesiosaurio aristonéctido que vivió en el Cretácico Inferior en lo que ahora es Rusia.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen was discovered in Chuvashia and dates to the late Hauterivian, approximately 133 to 130 million years ago.
facts.quote: El holotipo se encontró en Chuvashia, datando de fines del Hauteriviense en el Cretácico Inferior, hace unos 133-130 millones de años.

facts.statement: Abyssosaurus represents the first reliable record of an aristonectid plesiosaur in Russia.
facts.quote: Abyssosaurus representa el primer registro fiable de un aristonéctido en Rusia.

facts.statement: The genus was formally named by Alexander Yu. Berezin in 2011, with the type species designated as Abyssosaurus nataliae.
facts.quote: Abyssosaurus fue nombrado oficialmente por Alexander Yu. Berezin en 2011 y la especie tipo es Abyssosaurus nataliae.

facts.statement: Abyssosaurus is classified within the family Aristonectidae.
facts.quote: familia: Aristonectidae

facts.statement: The Paleobiology Database lists the parent group of Abyssosaurus as Cryptoclididae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Cryptoclididae

facts.statement: The time range for Abyssosaurus is recorded as the Hauterivian, spanning from 132.6 to 125.77 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Hauterivian to Hauterivian (132.6 to 125.77 million years ago)
